question: When setting out a complex roof with an irregular plan, which geometric principle is used to determine the true length of a hip rafter?
options: Pythagorean theorem applied to the plan length and total rise
Simple trigonometric sine rule applied to the pitch angle
The roof pitch multiplied by the span divided by two
The diagonal of the building plan multiplied by the common rafter factor

options: Ledged and braced doors
Six-panel Georgian doors with a bottom rail wider than the top rail
Flush doors with hardboard facing
Matchboarded doors with tongue and groove boards

options: Cosine of the pitch angle
Secant of the pitch angle
Tangent of the pitch angle

question: Which type of mortise and tenon joint is specifically used when joining a rail to a muntin where full depth cannot be achieved on both sides?
options: Stub tenon
Franked mortise and tenon
Twin tenon
Bare-faced tenon

The pitch angle and the plan angle only

options: BS 4978 visual stress grading

question: When setting out winding stairs (stairs with tapered treads), the 'pitch line' method requires that the going of each winder is measured at which specific position?

Along the centre line of the staircase flight
At the quarter point of the tread width

options: Reaction wood
Interlocked grain
Spiral grain

To establish the true shape of the face mould used to mark out the wreath
To calculate the number of balusters needed per winder

Urea formaldehyde (UF) resin
Resorcinol formaldehyde (RF) or melamine-urea formaldehyde (MUF) resin
Epoxy resin only when combined with mechanical fasteners

Vertical and horizontal datums, rebate positions, member sections, and joint locations
Material species, timber grade, and moisture content only

options: tan(backing bevel) = sin(α) × tan(θ)
tan(backing bevel) = cos(α) × tan(θ)
tan(backing bevel) = tan(α) / sin(θ)
